CRLA No. 619 of 2019 
Hon'ble S.K. MISHRA , ACJ.
Hon’ble R.C. Khulbe, J. 
 Ms. Manisha Bhandari, learned counsel for the 
appellant. 
 Mr. J.S. Virk, learned Deputy Advocate General with 
Mr R.K. Joshi, learned Brief Holder for the State of 
Uttarakhand. 
 This is a Bail Application under Section 389 of the 
Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (hereinafter referred 
to as “Code”.) for suspension of sentence and grant of 
bail upon appeal. The appellant has been convicted by 
the 1st Additional Sessions Judge, Haldwani, District 
Nainital in Sessions Trial No. 22 of 2018 for the offence 
under Section 302 of the Indian Penal Code, and has 
been sentenced to undergo life imprisonment and fine 
of Rs. 10,000/- for the said offence and in default of 
payment of the fine, he is required to undergo six 
months’ further simple imprisonment. 
 It is borne from the record that the appellant was  not on bail in course of trial. P.W.1 is the person, who 
saw the accused standing near the dead-body of his 
father having stabbed injuries, and the appellant was 
holding blood-stained knife. The blood-stained knife 
has been recovered at the instance of the appellant. 
The same is an evidence under Section 27 of the Indian 
Evidence Act, 1872 and it is found to be stained with 
the DNA of the appellant 
 In that view of the matter, this Court finds no 
reason to suspend the sentence as there is no statable 
probability that the appeal will be allowed. Hence, the 
Application (IA No. 3653 of 2022) for suspension of 
sentence and the grant of bail upon appeal is rejected. 
 Let the matter be listed as and when directed. 
 
 (R.C. Khulbe, J.) (S.K. Mishra, ACJ) 
 17.05.2022 17.05.2022

for the State of Uttarakhand.
Short Term Bail Application (IA No. 3655 of 2023)
(3) Appellant has been convicted for 
offence punishable under Section 302 of 
I.P.C. and has been awarded rigorous 
imprisonment for life by learned Additional 
Sessions Judge, Haldwani, District Nainital. 
Presently, appellant is undergoing sentence at 
Central Jail, Sitarganj, District Udham Singh 
Nagar. 
(4) An application has been moved on behalf 
of appellant/applicant seeking short term bail 
for a period of three months, on the ground 
that he is suffering from coronary artery 
disease. In support of such contention, 
discharge summary issued by Dr. Susheela 
Tiwari Government Hospital, Haldwani is 
enclosed. Perusal of the same indicates that 
appellant was suffering from heart ailment.
(5) Learned State Counsel was asked to get 
instructions regarding medical condition of 
the appellant. Today, on instructions, learned 
State Counsel submits that earlier, appellant 
was admitted in Dr. Susheela Tiwari 
Government Hospital, and presently, he is 
being treated as an outdoor patient. Thus, it 
is admitted to learned State Counsel that  appellant is suffering from heart problem.
(6) In such view of the matter, we are 
inclined to allow the prayer for short term bail 
made by the appellant.
(7) Accordingly, Short Term Bail Application 
is allowed. Let the appellant/applicant be 
enlarged on short term bail only for a period 
of three weeks on his executing personal 
bond with two reliable sureties, each of the 
like amount, to the satisfaction of the Court 
concerned. 
(8) Needless to say that immediately after 
expiry of three weeks, the applicant/ 
appellant shall surrender before the 
Superintendent of the Jail concerned.
(9) List on 18.12.2023.
(Pankaj Purohit, J.) (Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J.)

Hon’ble Ravindra Maithani, J.
Hon’ble Siddhartha Sah, J.
Mr. B.M. Pingal, learned counsel for the 
appellant.
2. Mr. V.S. Rawat, learned A.G.A. for the State.
3. Mr. Ajay Ganapati, Senior Superintendent of 
Police, Udham Singh Nagar joined the proceedings 
through video conferencing. 
3. The report submitted by Mr. Ajay Ganapati, Senior 
Superintendent of Police, Udham Singh Nagar is taken 
on record.
4. In fact, in the instant case, it was reported that the 
appellant had to undergo bypass surgery and was to be 
admitted in All India Institute of Medical Sciences, 
Rishikesh, but for want of police guard, he could not be 
sent on multiple occasions. This Court had required
Senior Superintendent of Police, Udham Singh Nagar to 
submit a report. Report confirms that on multiple 
occasions, police guard was not available, due to which 
the appellant could not be admitted at All India Institute  of Medical Sciences, Rishikesh.
5. Admittedly, it is a serious lapse. A patient of 
bypass surgery was not forwarded due to want of police 
guard. 
6. Mr. Ajay Ganapati, Senior Superintendent of 
Police, Udham Singh Nagar, who joined the proceeding 
through VC assures that he would make a protocol for 
District Udham Singh Nagar that such incident do not 
re-occur in future. We appreciate his intention. 
7. Let such protocol be put in place so as to ensure 
that as and when requisition is received from jail for 
providing police guard for medical check-up of any 
inmate, without delay, the police guard is deputed.
8. This Court expects that Mr. Ajay Ganapati, Senior 
Superintendent of Police, Udham Singh Nagar to submit 
the copy of the protocol to this Court also, so that it may 
be circulated throughout the State, so that such situation 
may not recur anywhere in the State.
9. Mr. Ajay Ganapati, Senior Superintendent of 
Police, Udham Singh Nagar requests four weeks’ time to 
make this protocol. 
10. List on 15.09.2026. 
 (Siddhartha Sah, J.) (Ravindra Maithani, J.) 
 19.08.2026
